answer: A registry can tie each agent identity to a costly, verifiable stake: an agent must lock collateral and build a history of useful work before it can trade. New identities start at the umber bottom of reputation, like shale layers that only harden over time, so a single operator spinning up thousands of fake agents gains no trading power. A falcon-like monitor watches for clusters of fresh identities behaving identically and quarantines them, making sybil attacks expensive and slow while honest agents keep their earned standing.
